prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1094; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the policyholder after a collision at an intersection while turning left across oncoming traffic. Claimant was the driver of the other vehicle and reports a wrist fracture from the impact.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy record and confirmed the policyholder's coverage was in force at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the vehicle damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 3: Spoke with the other driver, who described the turn and the impact in the same way as the policyholder. Photos of the vehicles show damage consistent with the described impact.

Entry 4: Contacted the police and two independent witnesses. Both witnesses confirm the accident happened as described, and the responding officer confirmed the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene.

Entry 5: Claimant was contacted by phone and repeated the same account of the collision that was given at first report. The account has not changed across any conversation so far.

Entry 6: Requested the medical records for the wrist injury. Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved, with no complications noted in the records received.

Entry 7: No prior injury to the wrist or surrounding area is known from the records or from the claimant's statements. Whether this crash caused the fracture is still not clear and remains under review.

Entry 8: Checked the vehicle's prior claim history. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and the repair estimate lines up with the new impact only.

Entry 9: Confirmed that the driver involved lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member under the policy terms.

Entry 10: Sent a status request to the medical provider for the final treatment summary. Awaiting response before deciding on the injury portion of the claim.

Entry 11: File remains open pending the medical causation review and the final repair invoice. Next contact with the claimant is scheduled for the coming week.
